business-data-context

Business data map

Bunkai TMS (staging database, 38 public tables, migrations 0001-0088). Entities, state machines, automatic processes, integrations and the flows that move data. Generated 2026-10-05 from the live staging schema, the target repo and the May 2026 legacy map.

Overview

Bunkai TMS is a multi-tenant test management system. A workspace (the tenant) holds projects; each project has a tree of modules (depth up to 6) that hold user stories and their acceptance criteria. QA authors ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases: titled, layered, stepped, traced to a story and at least one AC). ATCs are chained into workspace-scoped tests; a test is executed as a run against a project environment, and a failed run can raise a bug. Everything user-visible is also written to an activity log, which drives in-app and email notifications.

Actors: workspace roles viewer, member, admin, owner; personal access tokens (PAT) with scopes for agents and CI; Stripe (billing) and Resend (email) as machines. Plans: community, cloud, enterprise.

Data-layer conventions that apply everywhere: all 38 public tables have row level security on; no Postgres enums exist (every vocabulary is text plus a CHECK); writes go through 81 public functions, most SECURITY DEFINER RPCs named bunkai_* that take an actor id and check workspace role themselves; secrets live in separate *_secrets tables.

Entities

38 public tables (row counts are reltuples estimates from staging on 2026-10-05; staging also holds QA-created data, so counts are orders of magnitude only).

Key relationships: workspace to project (CASCADE); project to module (CASCADE); module to story (CASCADE); story to ATC is RESTRICT (a story with ATCs cannot be hard-deleted; it is archived instead); ATC to test is many-to-many through test_steps (atc_id RESTRICT, test_id CASCADE); test to run is RESTRICT; run to run_atcs to run_steps is CASCADE; bug links to run, run step and ATC are SET NULL so a bug outlives its evidence. Users reference auth.users; deleting a user SET NULLs authorship columns but RESTRICTs workspace ownership.

Workspaces: plan, seats and soft delete

  • plan is community | cloud | enterprise. New workspaces are created as community by bunkai_bootstrap_workspace (slug regex ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,38}[a-z0-9]$), with the caller inserted as owner/active.
  • Limits per plan (app constants in lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts): community 5 seats and 3 projects; cloud 25 seats, 50 projects, 2400 cents per seat; enterprise unlimited. The project limit is also enforced in the database by trigger (project_limit_reached, SQLSTATE 45700, limits 3 / 50 / none). The seat limit is app-side only: no database check was found.
  • purchased_seats is NULL until a paid upgrade, then > 0.
  • deleted_at non-NULL means the workspace is in its 30-day deletion window; bunkai_workspace_is_live is the predicate policies use. See flow-workspace-deletion.
  • Roles in workspace_members.role: viewer, member, admin, owner. Invites can only grant viewer, member or admin.

Modules: materialized path and archive cascade

  • path is a slash-separated materialized path; a CHECK limits depth to 1-6 segments. bunkai_move_module and bunkai_update_module (rename or new slug) maintain it.
  • Modules, user stories, acceptance criteria and ATCs have archived_at. bunkai_archive_module_subtree archives the module, its active descendants, their stories, those stories' ACs and the ATCs in scope in one call, and writes module.archived with the four counts. Archiving an already archived module returns zeros and writes no audit row.
  • Archived rows are hidden, not deleted: atcs.user_story_id RESTRICT means hard delete of a story that has ATCs is impossible.

ATCs: versioning, classification and traceability

  • layer is UI | API | Unit. technique (optional) is one of Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis, State Transition, Decision Table, Pairwise. priority (optional) is Critical | High | Medium | Low. Technique and priority were added in migration 0087 (the May map predates them).
  • status CHECK allows pass, fail, blocked, skipped, running, unrun. The migrations/RPCs read here never set it; who writes it is unverified (see discovery-gaps).
  • version starts at 1 and increments on every bunkai_update_atc. The caller passes If-Match (p_if_match); a mismatch raises version_conflict:<current> (SQLSTATE 45022). Steps, assertions and AC links are replaced wholesale on update.
  • At least one AC is required and every AC must belong to the ATC's own story and be un-archived (ac_outside_user_story, 45020). Tags capped at 10 (atc_tags_limit_exceeded, 45024). Title minimum 3 characters is a NOT VALID check (applies to new writes only; legacy rows may be shorter).
  • A search vector tsv is refreshed by trigger on title or tags change and feeds bunkai_search_atcs.
  • Because tests reference ATCs by id, updating an ATC changes what every test that chains it will run next; the audit payload lists affected_test_ids.

Tests and runs: chains and snapshots

  • A tests row belongs to a workspace (not a project). Its chain is test_steps(position >= 1, atc_id). A test's project is derived from its ATCs; bunkai_create_run picks the first distinct project and the module of the ATC at position 1.
  • Tags go through bunkai_normalize_test_tags and a shape CHECK; version is bumped by tag and step reorder RPCs that also take If-Match.
  • A run snapshots test title, each ATC title and every step's content, input and expected at start; later ATC edits do not alter past runs. atc_id and atc_step_id on the snapshot are SET NULL if the source disappears.
  • executor_mode is human | agent | ci. start_token (1-200 chars) makes creation idempotent: the same (test_id, start_token) inside 24 hours returns the existing run with replayed: true.
  • abort_reason is required (3-500 chars) when status is aborted and must be NULL otherwise (CHECK).

Secret isolation pattern

Three token families (PATs, magic links, invites) each store metadata in one table and the secret material in a sibling *_secrets table (FK CASCADE, RLS on). Metadata can be shown to users; the secrets table is not meant to be readable through the API. PATs expose only token_prefix; scopes are a CHECK-constrained subset of atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin with at least one required. Revocation sets revoked_at; rows are never deleted by the app.

Flow: authoring (project to ATC)

  1. User or PAT (atc:write) creates a project: bunkai_enforce_project_limit may reject with 45700.
  2. Creates modules (depth at most 6), then a user story (status draft), then acceptance criteria (bunkai_insert_acceptance_criterion, bunkai_move_acceptance_criterion keep position dense).
  3. bunkai_create_atc inserts the ATC plus steps, assertions and AC links in one transaction, after checking the actor can write the project and the ACs belong to the story. A slug is derived per project.
  4. bunkai_set_user_story_status moves the story to ready_to_test.
  5. Every step writes activity_log (for example atc.updated, module.archived).

Entities touched: modules, user_stories, acceptance_criteria, atcs and children, activity_log.

Flow: running a test

  1. bunkai_create_run(actor, test, environment, executor_mode, start_token): needs write access to the test's workspace; environment must belong to the test's project (environment_invalid, 45201); a test with no ATC steps raises no_executable_steps (45202). Locks the project row, replays on token reuse, then inserts runs (status running), one run_atcs per chain position and one run_steps per ATC step, all pending. Logs run.started.
  2. bunkai_mark_run_step accepts only passed | failed | blocked (45213) while the run is running (run_step_marking_closed, 45212), stores note, evidence URL and executed_at, then recomputes the parent run_atcs.status: any pending leaves it pending; else any failed gives failed; else any blocked gives blocked; else passed. Logs run_step.marked.
  3. Finish: bunkai_finish_run(verdict) takes passed | failed (45207), sets status and finished_at, bumps version, marks every still-pending step and chain position skipped, logs run.finished. bunkai_abort_run(reason, via) does the same with status aborted and a mandatory reason, logging run.aborted. Finishing a non-running run raises run_not_finishable (45206).
  4. The verdict is chosen by the caller; it is not derived from step results by the database.
  5. Abandoned runs are closed by the sweep (see automatic-processes). The run-event trigger then creates a notification for the executor.

Flow: reporting and handling a bug

  1. bunkai_create_bug inserts status open with title (trimmed, 5-200 chars), severity P1-P4, steps to reproduce (required), up to 10 evidence URLs, and optional run, run step and ATC.
  2. The bugs_check_consistency trigger rejects cross-scope links: project outside workspace (45304), module outside project (45300), run outside project (45305), run step outside the given run (45306), ATC outside project (45307).
  3. bunkai_assign_bug sets assignee_user_id; the assignee must be an active member and not a viewer (45312, 45313). Logs bug.assigned, bug.reassigned or bug.unassigned.
  4. bunkai_transition_bug_status moves one step forward at a time (see state-bug) and logs bug.status_changed with previous status and assignee snapshot.
  5. Those four audit actions fire bunkai_notify_bug_event, which creates notifications.

Flow: invitation and membership

Owner or admin creates a workspace_invites row (email, role viewer | member | admin) plus its secret row. Acceptance sets accepted_by_user_id/accepted_at and inserts a workspace_members row. Invite lifecycle is derived from timestamps (pending, accepted, revoked, expired), not from a status column. bunkai_leave_workspace lets a member leave; membership status is active | invited | suspended. The invite acceptance function and its email path were not read in this run (see discovery-gaps).

Flow: upgrade to Cloud

  1. App starts a checkout: inserts billing_checkout_sessions (target plan always cloud, seat quantity > 0 and within the plan bounds, unique idempotency key, expires_at) and creates a Stripe Checkout Session; a stale open row may be flipped to expired locally and reused.
  2. Stripe calls the webhook; bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event locks the session row. Replays of an already completed row return already_processed; an expired or canceled row still accepts a genuinely paid completed event; a repeated Stripe event id returns duplicate through the stripe_webhook_events ledger.
  3. On checkout.session.completed or async_payment_succeeded with payment status paid: workspaces.plan and purchased_seats are set, the session row becomes completed, and workspace.plan_upgraded is logged (actor NULL). Other payment statuses return awaiting_payment; async_payment_failed and expired mark an open row expired.

Flow: workspace data export

Owner only (lib/workspace-export/authorize.ts). A workspace_exports row (queued, running, completed, failed) is inserted; its insert trigger logs the request. The runner builds an archive into the private storage bucket workspace-exports (no storage policy for anon or authenticated), and bunkai_resolve_workspace_export_download resolves a download. The download window is 168 hours from readiness (EXPORT_DOWNLOAD_WINDOW_HOURS).

Flow: workspace deletion with 30-day grace

  1. bunkai_request_workspace_deletion: owner only (45900); already deleted raises 45901. Sets deleted_at and deletion_requested_by, revokes every live PAT of the workspace, revokes pending invites, writes a workspace_deletions ledger row (purge deadline now plus 30 days, member count, row-count digest of projects, tests, runs, bugs, members) and returns recipient emails for the notification mail.
  2. bunkai_restore_workspace_deletion cancels within the window. Revoked tokens and invites are not un-revoked by the code read here.
  3. The nightly purge hard-deletes the workspace (all child rows cascade) and stamps purged_at. See automatic-processes.

Flow: Jira import

An import_jobs row stores the JQL, status (queued, running, completed, failed), paging token and counters (imported, created, updated, skipped, errors jsonb). lib/jira/import-runner.ts pages through Jira, extracts acceptance criteria from descriptions (ADF to Markdown) and upserts user stories keyed by external_id, filling external_url. The runner is app code, not a database process. Import details beyond the table shape were not traced (see discovery-gaps).

Flow: audit event to notification

  1. An RPC writes activity_log.
  2. Run (run.finished, run.aborted) and bug (assigned, reassigned, unassigned, status_changed) events fire triggers that insert notifications for the recipient, deduplicated by unique (source_event_id, recipient_user_id). A run event is skipped when the recipient is the actor and payload.via = 'cookie' (you do not get told about your own click), or when the run has no executor.
  3. Preferences: event_type in run_lifecycle | bug_lifecycle | mentions, channel in in_app | email.
  4. Daily at 08:00 UTC Vercel cron calls /api/v1/admin/send-digest, which uses bunkai_notification_digest_candidates, sends through Resend and records notification_digest_log (pending, sent, failed).

State: run

FromToEventEffects
(none)runningbunkai_create_runSnapshot rows created, all pending; run.started.
runningpassed or failedbunkai_finish_run (caller verdict)Pending steps and chain positions become skipped; run.finished; version+1.
runningabortedbunkai_abort_run or inactivity sweepReason required; skipped fan-out; run.aborted (sweep: actor NULL, via='sweep').
passed, failed, aborted(terminal)anyNo transition out: finish raises 45206, step marking raises 45212.

Step grain: run_steps pending to passed | failed | blocked (marking) or skipped (closing). Chain-position grain (run_atcs): derived as described in flow-test-execution, plus skipped on closure.

State: bug

FromToEventEffects
openin_progressbunkai_transition_bug_statusbug.status_changed with previous status and assignee snapshot; notification.
in_progressresolvedsamesame
resolvedclosedsamesame
anynon-adjacent or earliersame, or direct UPDATERejected: 45310 skip, 45311 backward. There is no reopen path in the database.

The same rank check lives in the RPC (friendly errors) and in the bugs_check_consistency trigger (backstop for direct writes).

Integration: Supabase (Auth, Postgres, Storage)

The spine. Auth provides auth.users (referenced by 20+ FKs) and sessions; magic link and email plus password both exist (auth_email_status RPC). Postgres holds all data with RLS everywhere; privileged logic is SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = ''. Storage holds only the private workspace-exports bucket. If Supabase is down nothing works; there is no fallback path.

Integration: Stripe

Outbound: create Checkout Sessions for the Cloud plan. Inbound: signed webhook events, recorded in stripe_webhook_events (~310 rows) for exactly-once application. Failure behaviour: if the webhook is missed, the checkout row stays open and the workspace stays on its old plan although the customer paid; a redelivered event repairs it. Dependent flow: flow-billing-upgrade.

Integration: Resend (email)

Now wired (the May map called it declared but unwired): used by the daily digest and the workspace-deletion notice. Configured by RESEND_API_KEY. Failure behaviour: the digest log row goes to failed; a missed deletion email does not stop the deletion because the RPC has already committed.

Integration: Jira (import)

Inbound only: import_jobs pull stories and acceptance criteria by JQL into user_stories.external_id/external_url. The May map listed Jira as dev tooling only; it is now a product feature. A Jira outage fails or stalls the job; already imported data is unaffected.

Discovery gaps

  • I could not read cron.job on staging (permission denied for schema cron): schedules come from migrations 0075 and 0084, activity on staging is unverified.
  • I could not verify who writes atcs.status (pass, fail, blocked, skipped, running, unrun). No function read here sets it; the run flow tracks status on runs, run_atcs and run_steps.
  • Not read in detail: invite creation and acceptance, magic-link issuance, bunkai_create_atc slug derivation, test plan RPCs (default status, close transition), milestone semantics, feature_flags consumers, user_view_state contents, Jira import field mapping, idempotency key lifecycle beyond the status vocabulary.
  • Seat limits (5 / 25 / unlimited) were found only in app constants; no database enforcement was seen.
  • RLS policies were confirmed enabled on all 38 tables but individual policy predicates were not dumped.
  • Row counts are planner estimates and staging contains QA-generated data; they say nothing about production volume. Production has no database access in this repo (single MVP database phase per the target's AGENTS.md).
  • The legacy May 2026 map described 8 migrations and triggers only on atcs; this map supersedes it. Legacy sections on PAT lifecycle, dual-mode auth and headless sign-up were not re-traced (they belong to business-api-context).
